items.note: Association organized at Larrow Green 1889; Gideon Vose president 1889-1911; creamery built 1891 (story 1).
Article VII: paid by butterfat by test, not by weight; 'the test of the station where he delivers shall govern' (story 1).
'Under payment by weight a short pipette would have cost nobody anything' (story 1).
Effie Loomis secretary 1901-, Teague bookkeeper 1905-, Sill buttermaker (story 1).
Selby Vose, Gideon's son, manager from 1913 (story 1).
Station-gain line: yearly, 1898 entry already 'as usual', 5 1/4 percent, carried to general account (story 8).
Ostrey Hollow station, 7 miles up valley, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green (stories 1-2).
Milk weighed in, composite jars, fixed 17.6 c.c. charge, fat read on neck graduated for the full charge (stories 2-3).
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897 (story 3).
Full invoice table, 6 doz pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., total $77.93 (story 3).
'The gap was a flat 0.19, the same in July as in February' (story 6).
Section A never says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, or that the county had none. The 'one instrument a plant cannot check' point appears only in Section F.
Ansel Keddie 1861-1934, twenty-nine seasons 1896-1924, dismissed 30 April 1925 (story 2).
Bench routine; five-column book in his own hand; errors crossed out and initialled (story 2).
1896 3.80 on borrowed glass; 3.61 +/-0.03 from 1898 (story 2).
8 May to 10 July 1911, borrowed measure, 3.80, question mark (story 2).
Orra, Emmet's sister, married Ansel; the tester was married to the sister of the patron who lost most (story 4).

1919 circular signed by Vose alone (story 5); 17 March 1925 statement that he could not say why the figures were what they were and took no cream (story 2). Leaves out 'tested as he was taught', but the statement and its core are there.
Died Feb 1934 uncleared; book impounded March 1925, at Historical Rooms since 1959 (story 2).
Hessel Bottom, six farms, Emmet Brant's the largest (story 4).
Weigh book from 1 January 1897; the weights always agreed (story 4).
Complaints from about 1902 (story 6); the 0.17 against Larrow Green's 3.78 is kept separate from the 0.19 true shortfall (story 4). Never gives Hollow-vs-Green as 0.19.
Grigg committee sampled Jan-Mar 1908 and blamed hay, stated as the committee's finding (story 6).
1910: 200,000 lb on 3.42 (story 4); error proportional to richness (story 3).
Roy from 1929, lent to Ivy 1958, Hazel from 1962 (story 4).
Cudd's cheese factory at Alder Corners, Vessey County, over Redlow Ridge; first season 1914. The year does not gate. The 1913 'built' date takes a deduction separately.
From 1915 four Bottom men hauled summer milk over the ridge (story 7).
His own new glass, compared with no one's, in Vessey County; 'independent control' (story 7).
In every overlap season the same men's milk tested 3.80 over the ridge against 3.61 at the station, a gap of 0.19; sixteen seasons 1915-1930 (story 7).
Same cows' summer milk, different glass: defeats both hay and water (story 7).
Rosalie, Jerome's daughter, took over in 1941 and copied the figures for Ivy in 1958 (story 7).
Strawn, Ordell circuit 1907-March 1936, kin to nobody, a notebook each year (story 5).
Lactometer on every visit, never found water (story 5).
12 June 1923, against a burette, 'Condemned the lot, the whole crate' (story 3).
Never says Strawn wrote no figure for the deficiency, made no report beyond the condemnation, or drew no inference about the years before.
Gives the 28 June order, the 2 July acknowledgement, July in use and 1924 at 3.80. The gated clause 'nobody connected the rise with the condemnation' is never stated in Section A.
Crate to the station loft (story 3); notebooks to the state office in 1936 and Farland library in 1947, where Ivy found the 1923 volume (story 5).
Petition January 1925 (story 8).
Frick board, 17 March-4 May 1925, three sittings, two in the station weigh room (story 8).
Water (Vose), theft (Teague), hay (1908 report); none established (story 8).
'Four books and nothing else', Strawn's 1923 notebook among them; 'Nobody laid those books side by side' (story 8); the 1923 volume holds the condemnation (stories 3, 5).
Dismissed 30 April 1925 with no finding; $3,800 'without admission' on 4 May, charged to station account (stories 2, 8).
Gives the one-fifth of $19,000, but never says the award was charged to the account the loss had built up in as 'gain'. The run in fact puts the gain in the general account.
Ivy, born 1931, Duncan's daughter and Orra's granddaughter; graduate student at the State Agricultural College at Farland with Vaught (stories 3-4).
Section A never says Ivy put together records that had never been in the same room. That synthesis appears only in the Section G summary.
February 1958 she found the crate (stored in the loft), nine survived (story 3).
9 March 1958, calibrated burette, 16.72 vs 17.6, 0.88 short, 95% (story 3).
One part in twenty low from 1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923 (story 3); 3.61 for 3.80, 0.19 (stories 2, 7).
Has 40M lb, 76,000 lb and $19,000 at 25 cents (story 8), but no identity between the 76,000 and the sum of station-gain entries. REQUIRED needs all four.
Bulletin 471, October 1958; 24 years after death, 33 after dismissal (story 2); 35 years after condemnation (story 3).
Granddaughter via Duncan; great-niece rejected.

Second cousins, derived: 1. Abstention A08: 'The two nearest witnesses say full, so I take full, but it is not proven'; E35 resolves '-> Full'. It also claims a half-sibling would make them 'half second cousins', not that the answer is unchanged. 0 on the second point.
Gideon, father; wrote Article VII, which made the station's test decisive, so Selby was defending his father's rule.
Abstention A01 asserted: 'nothing supports one, and I answer: none.' Treats Duncan's denial as settling it. Asserting either way = 0.
0.95, 5%, one part in twenty.
$86.40 at 24 cents.
76,000; 5.00% of fat received/delivered and 5.26% of fat credited, both denominators named.
$77.93 with the sum.
72 pipettes; 0.88 c.c. each.
26 years 1 month 11 days (about 26 years 6 weeks) against 25 full years 1898-1922; part years given as the reason.
Abstention A02: cannot be determined; two memories and no document.
Variable: the measuring pipette.
Tester, bottles, acid, hand tester, scale, patrons, herds, hay.
About 3.80 for nine weeks, back to 3.61 on 10 July.
Water, theft and hay ruled out, cause at the station glass; limits include how short each pipette was and whose measure it was.
Ledger/Sill, 1911 interval/Keddie, Strawn, Alder Corners/Rosalie: several narrators, each attributed.
Independence argued; ledger and 1911 hold without the 1958 measurement.
Abstention A09: 'Whether that 1916 conversation happened cannot be settled'; Teague and Kyle's accounts contrasted.
Yes, he knew the tests ran low: 1919 circular, complaints since 1902.
Manager from 1913, signed the station-gain sheets, wrote the 1919 circular.
Abstention A03: whether he understood cannot be determined; no source shows he connected the line; signature/thumb (signing is not reading).
Rows 2 (1908 sampling), 3 (1924 average), 5 (weigh book), 6 (six farms), 7 (Orra 1866), 9 (crate in loft), each resolved with a method.
Near-tie table: NT-1 16.27, NT-11 12 July (28 June order), NT-14 $77.39, and more, each with a tie-breaker.
A04 (works books burned 1931), A06 (ND, Roy's version sits badly with the dates), A10 (by-laws undated, minute book lost).
Self-refutations: r15, r18, r20, r07, r05, r03, r11.
16.72/17.6 = 0.95; proportional 0.19 on 3.80; onset 1 May 1897 against 1896 at 3.80; end 12 June 1923 against 1924 at 3.80; nothing else changed.
Water (Vose, Sill), defeated by Strawn's lactometer and Alder Corners.
Theft (Teague), defeated by cream arriving heavy in the ledger, plus 1911 and 1924.
Hay (Grigg, Kepp), defeated by Bulletin 214's 0.05 winter / nil summer against a flat 0.19.
Abstention A07 asserted: 'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glass? No.'
Abstention A05: 'This cannot be determined.'
143 words.
Test book, Brant weigh book, Strawn's notebook, ledger, Alder Corners tests, invoice, 1958 measurement.
Decoys given as what the valley blamed, not as fact; no wrong headline figures.
1897, 5% low, 76,000 lb/$19,000, 1923, 1958, Ansel and Ivy: both ends covered.

deductions.reason: Gullibility A08 (B2/E35): 'so I take full' and '-> Full'; asserts Orra was Emmet's full sister.
Gullibility A01 (B4): 'I answer: none'; asserts no Vose-Keddie kinship.
Gullibility A07 (F5, also E44): asserts the 1925 board did not examine the glass.
Corruption NT-13/F044: 'Keddie went up in 1895 to make the new skimming station ready' and story range '(1895-1934)'; puts the planted 1895 start into a harmonized story as fact.
Corruption F055: 'Jerome Cudd built a cheese factory at Alder Corners ... in 1913' stated as fact (E22 'built 1913, first season 1914').
